pr_title: lightning: use pd timestamp to update gc safepoint
pr_body:

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and 
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/32733

Problem Summary:

Lightning uses the local unix timestamp to update service gc safepoint. However, local clock is not reliable. If the start ts of checksum transaction is smaller than the local ts, lightning may encounter “GC life time is shorter than transaction duration” error during doing checksum.

### What is changed and how it works?

Always use PD timestamp to update service gc safepoint.

issue_context.title: lightning: checksum encountered  “GC life time is shorter than transaction duration”  error
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

Use Lightning to import about 5T data.

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

Data was imported successfully.

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

checksum encountered  “GC life time is shorter than transaction duration”  error.
```
[2022/02/25 21:01:06.846 +00:00] [ERROR] [lightning.go:219] ["tidb lightning encountered error"] [error="[tikv:9006]GC life time is shorter than transaction duration, transaction starts at 2022-02-25 20:44:20.986 +0000 UTC, GC safe point is 2022-02-25 20:44:21 +0000 UTC"] [errorVerbose="[tikv:9006]GC life time is shorter than transaction duration, transaction starts at 2022-02-25 20:44:20.986 +0000 UTC, GC safe point is 2022-02-25 20:44:21 +0000 UTC
```

### 4. What is your TiDB-Lightning version? (Required)

v5.3.0

review_comments: if fetch TSO failed should we fallback to using local timestamp rather than failing? 🤔
This TSO will be also used for checksum executor which seems to be required. Anyway, it can't be any worse than before.
